messages:
sana: Heads-up — customer Pavo reported garbled outputs after we merged their LoRA + int4 quant profile this morning. emojis and some bracketed numeric tokens get mangled, e.g. "I love this 😊" -> "I love this ðŸ˜Š". Anyone seen this pattern with merges before?

liam: Ugh. Can you paste a minimal failing example and which model variant you used?

sana: Sure — example from their quick-eval pack 2026-03-20 run:
```
INPUT: 'Show me the emoji summary: 😊 ->'
BASE (fp16): 'Summary: happy face 😊'
MERGED+int4: 'Summary: happy face ðŸ˜Š'
MERGED+int8: 'Summary: happy face 😊'
```
We used prod/redwood-v2-large + pavo-lora-v1 merged, quant profile int4-qs8. Eval pack id: pavo_quick_0316.

owen: That looks like a tokenizer/encoding mismatch — typical when LoRA was trained with a slightly different tokenizer or an intermediate patch changed unicode-normalization. Quick check: did the adapter specify 'preserve_unicode: true' in merge metadata?

maya: I pulled the merge manifest — adapter metadata has tokenizer_version: 2025-09-crypto-bpe, main model uses tokenizer_version: 2025-09-bpe (no crypto). So slight mismatch.

liam: Nice catch. That explains why fp16 and int8 still map correctly in some paths (different kernel paths sometimes re-normalize). int4 path probably uses a faster token decode that doesn't normalize.

zara: Repro steps I ran locally:
```bash
# reproduce quick eval locally
python infra/eval/runner.py --model prod/redwood-v2-large --adapter pavo-lora-v1 --quant int4-qs8 --eval-set pavo_quick_0316 --out /tmp/pavo-int4.json
```
Output matches customer's failure.

owen: Plan: 1) revert the merged adapter on prod 2) run tokenizer_compare to diff tokenization of sample inputs 3) re-generate a remapped adapter (rebase tokens) or force adapter to store tokenizer alias in metadata 4) re-run quick-eval pack and smoke. Anyone object?

liam: +1. Can we try a quick remap before revert? If remap script succeeds in <30m we can avoid a rollback.

sana: I'll kick off tokenizer_compare now and post diffs. If remap fails, revert and open a hotfix adapter build.

ci-bot: build/pavo-lora-remap-job triggered by sana — job id: build-8427 — estimated 12m.

maya: If we do revert, let's also gate the adapter merges with a small token-normalization check in the CI quickpack so this doesn't slip again. I can add a tokenizer sanity test to the merge pipeline.

zara: Also recommend adding one targeted unit in the quick-eval that asserts emoji round-trip equality for common emojis. That caught this last time in other customers.

nowen: (typo fix) oops meant 'nowen' is me — ignoring. :facepalm:

owen: Results from tokenizer_compare (partial):
- sample '😊' encoded bytes differ: adapter-> [0xF0,0x9F,0x98,0x8A] vs main-> normalized to single token id 34567
- map mismatch for sequences starting with U+FE0F variation selectors

liam: Given that, remap likely to succeed but we should run the remapped adapter through int4 quant path locally before promoting.

sana: build-8427 finished: remap step succeeded, artifacts at gs://redwood-artifacts/pavo/remap-8427.tar.gz. Kicking local int4 smoke now.

zara: Local int4 smoke: 60/60 prompts pass emoji roundtrip. Quick-eval full pack queued.

ci-bot: pavo_quick_0316 re-eval started by zara — run id: eval-9921.

liam: If eval-9921 looks clean, let's ship remapped adapter and patch CI to include the tokenization check. I'll prep a short PR. :thumbsup:

sana: Thanks everyone — will update customer and keep thread open until we confirm no regression in their next deploy. :eyes:
